daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

PDI-P announced it will dismiss Klaten Regent Hamenang on Monday following his arrest by the Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK). The KPK detained the regent and a regional BPK official in an operation related to a Rp 600 million request to condition financial reports, with funds allegedly used to repay election debts and stored in barrels. PDI-P Secretary General Hasto Kristiyanto emphasized the party has zero tolerance for corruption.

  • The DPR faces a dilemma in responding to Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's diploma requirement controversy.
  • Vice President Ma'ruf Amin visited Sekolah Rakyat (People's School) sites, acknowledging initial doubts but noting promising prospects, and later invited students to pray for President Prabowo's success.
  • Deputy Minister of Education Gus Ipul reported that 182 Sekolah Rakyat centers are now operational, accommodating more than 44,000 students.
  • DPR members expressed concern that halting school meal programs during distance learning could disrupt student nutrition, though some legislators suggested parents could collect meals from schools.
  • A DPR member responded to the National Police Chief's proposal for an MUI fatwa on vaping products.
  • Army Chief of Staff General Tandyo presided over handover ceremonies for deputy KSAD, Kostrad commander, and regional military commanders.
  • A PLT Bupati in Gowa plans to reactivate regional officials previously dismissed by former regent Husniah Talenrang.

Foreign Policy & Defence

UN Secretary-General António Guterres arrived in Indonesia, welcomed by the Foreign Minister, with a scheduled meeting with President Prabowo planned to strengthen multilateral cooperation. The visit comes as Indonesia continues to position itself as a key player in global diplomacy and multilateral institutions.

  • President Prabowo hosted a dinner with Russia's Deputy Prime Minister in Bogor, gathering ministers for the meeting.
  • Russian President Vladimir Putin sent birthday greetings to President Prabowo on his 75th birthday.
  • Indonesia and Rosatom agreed on a project for electricity export from a floating nuclear power plant.
  • Indonesia and Russia are exploring collaboration in shipbuilding and aviation sectors.
  • At a UNESCO session, Indonesia advocated for child protection in the AI era.
  • Indonesia's Foreign Ministry was urged to take a stance after former U.S. President Trump used the name "Mohammad" in jokes.

Other

Indonesia's food sector has strengthened as Prabowo's government marks two years in office, according to Bapanas. The agency highlighted improvements in food security and agricultural productivity across the archipelago. Meanwhile, Indonesia extended the halal certification mandate for select sectors to October 2028, with LPPOM MUI urging businesses not to wait for deadlines.

  • The government is monitoring haze risks to flights at 16 Papua airports, while BNPB deployed 2.4 tons of dry ice to clear South Sumatra haze and flights were cancelled at Palu airport due to haze and tailwinds.
  • MUI called for perpetrators of forest fires to be prosecuted without exception, while Singapore identified seven Indonesian companies allegedly responsible for the fires.
  • Indonesia and Senegal chambers signed a pact to boost trade and investment, while the country is eyeing export expansion in six West African nations and exploring cassava processing investment in Mozambique.
  • Indonesia recorded US$4.84 billion in trade with Russia in 2025.
  • ASDP and Parameswara are studying a proposed ferry route between Dumai and Melaka.
  • Pertamina is ramping up fuel recovery in Bali, targeting 48 million liters.
